config.title: Platform Credentials

config.bot_usernames_fill_hint: Fill manually or auto-fill from verification result

config.devstage_hint: AI DevSpace default spec (3c6g/ARM); leave blank to keep current value. env GRAPE_DEVSTAGE_* overrides
config.webhook_url_hint: Public base URL (no platform path): the callback path is appended from the platform card as /webhook/<platform>; any /webhook/xxx here is ignored
config.webhook_url_ph: Public webhook callback URL of this service (deployment-level, shared by all platforms)

field_docs.name: Display name (list and login button text)
field_docs.dialect: API dialect family: github = GitHub-style REST; gitee v5 platforms follow the gitcode form
field_docs.host: Platform domain (clone URLs and page redirects)
field_docs.webhook_path: Route path this service receives the platform webhook on (e.g. /webhook/gitee)
field_docs.api_base: REST API base URL (upstream calls from the proxy layer)
field_docs.api_auth: Auth shape: query_token = v5 query param / token_header = GitHub header / private_token = GitLab header / bearer_header = Bearer
field_docs.webhook_verify: Webhook verification: token_compare = plain compare / hmac = HMAC-SHA256
field_docs.webhook_dialect: Webhook function-family dispatch key (github_web / gitee_v5; new platforms reuse a family by declaring it)
field_docs.clone_auth: git clone credential shape: basic_password / x_access_token
field_docs.bot_username: Bot account name on this platform (self-comment detection and collaborator invites)
field_docs.brand_color: Brand color (icon tinting, login buttons and other consumers)
field_docs.pat_create_url: User PAT creation page link (guidance redirect)
field_docs.token_env: Token environment variable name (deployment-level fallback read)
field_docs.legacy_token_symbol: Legacy token getter symbol name (compat marker, no behavior change)
field_docs.redirect_uri: OAuth callback URL (full URL incl. path; empty = derived from Host header)
field_docs.id_field: Field name of the platform user id in user info
field_docs.login_field: Field name of the login name in user info
field_docs.name_field: Field name of the display name in user info
field_docs.email_field: Field name of the email in user info
field_docs.accept_header: API Accept header (v5 family requires it explicitly)
field_docs.pkce_enabled: OAuth PKCE hardening (S256; recommended for public clients)
field_docs.issue_write_form: Issue write endpoint shape: repo_path = /repos/{o}/{r}/issues; owner_param = /repos/{o}/issues + repo in body (v5 family)
field_docs.branch_create_form: Branch creation shape: form = form body / refs_sha = refs param + sha
field_docs.pr_comment_endpoint: PR comment endpoint: pulls = /pulls/{n}/comments; issues = issues/{n}/comments (github /pulls is the inline-review endpoint)
field_docs.pr_labels_via_issues: PR labels edited via the issues endpoint (github PATCH /pulls rejects labels)
field_docs.pr_head_filter: PR list head filter shape: owner_ref = owner-prefixed / bare_ref = bare branch name
field_docs.git_tree_family: Tree API family: github_api = default_branch field + recursive trees + ref-name direct; v5 = branches[0] + commits?sha precheck + recursive rejected
field_docs.workflows_write: Push workflows file permission (set false when the GitHub App token lacks it)
field_docs.owner_identity_token_fallback: Final fallback after the standard token strategy chain: look up the repo owner's platform identity (legacy hosting compat semantics)
field_docs.milestone_verify_readback: GET readback verification after milestone writes (guards upstream silent ignores, compare + rollback on failure)
field_docs.milestone_id_resolve_to_number: Resolve milestone_id to the upstream milestone number before writing (guards id/number misuse)
field_docs.milestone_due_on_required: due_on required on milestone creation (guards v5 upstream 400, local readable interception)
field_docs.milestone_due_date_only: due_on accepts YYYY-MM-DD only (ISO timestamps truncated)
field_docs.milestone_due_time_only: due_on accepts ISO datetime only (pure dates padded to T00:00:00Z)
field_docs.closing_refs_auto_close_default: Closing keywords (Closes #N) auto-close upstream; auto_close defaults to true
field_docs.labels_array_form: Issue labels must be an array (comma strings get upstream 422)
field_docs.labels_color_prefix_hash: Label colors must be hex with # prefix
field_docs.issue_body_repo_bare: Issue write body repo field = bare repo name (not owner/repo)
field_docs.pr_comment_id_hex: PR comment id is 32-hex (resolved to numeric note_id before writes)
field_docs.legacy_repo_token_getter: Legacy four-level fallback repo-token read chain (compat period)
field_docs.token_storage_field: managed_repos bot-token column. Empty = credentials only in grape_t_repo_credentials (F4 terminal); a column name enables the legacy column (gitcode/github compat only)
field_docs.webhook_token_field: managed_repos webhook-token column. Empty = credentials only in grape_t_repo_credentials (F4 terminal); a column name enables the legacy column
field_docs.global_bot_meta_key: Meta storage key of the global bot token
field_docs.global_bot_status_meta_key: Meta storage key of the global bot token expiry status

type.note: ⚠ Only oidc has id_token claims fallback.

auth_url.note: All three endpoints are required; a card missing one is rejected.

token_url.note: Wrong endpoint shows up as token exchange failure.

user_url.note: ⚠ Huawei needs the token as a query parameter.

emails_endpoint.note: Empty means this channel provides no email.

scope.note: ⚠ Changing it affects every link of this channel; Gitee requires the exact scope set and a matching previous grant; insufficient scope makes repo calls return SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT.

pkce_enabled.note: ⚠ Gitee must keep this false, otherwise the consent page shows every login.

login_field.note: Falls back to external id when missing.

name_field.note: Empty falls back to the login name.

avatar_field.note: Empty uses the platform default rule.

redirect_uri.note: Empty derives from server_base_url; a wrong value gives redirect_uri_mismatch.

accept_header.note: GitHub returns legacy fields without it.

repo_links.what: Repo platforms this channel may drive (read-only).
repo_links.note: A configured pair lets that channel's token drive the platform (login writes the user-platform relation). No tier field exists; deleting the pair stops driving.

bot_username.note: ⚠ The single bot account of this platform; its token lives in bot_token_enc (encrypted).

enabled.what: Whether the object is enabled (DB authoritative).
enabled.note: ⚠ Config files never override it; import never touches this column.

dialect.note: ⚠ Same family covers several platforms (gitcode/gitee/github all use github).

host.note: Do not put the API base here.

api_base.note: Do not put the web host here.

webhook_path.note: Must match the platform webhook config.

webhook_verify.note: ⚠ hmac verifies a signature; token_compare compares a URL token.

webhook_dialect.note: ⚠ Must be declared; hosting is fail-closed when missing.

pr_head_filter.note: ⚠ Wrong form returns an empty list silently.

client_id.what: OAuth app client_id (encrypted column, only a boolean is returned).
client_id.values: copy from the platform app page
client_id.note: ⚠ Empty keeps the current value; plaintext is never readable again.

client_secret.what: OAuth app client_secret (encrypted column, only a boolean is returned).
client_secret.values: copy from the platform app page
client_secret.note: ⚠ Empty keeps the current value; fill the new one to rotate.

enabled_channel.what: Whether this login channel accepts logins (DB is authoritative).
enabled_channel.note: ⚠ When off, the login entry answers 403 CHANNEL_DISABLED (already signed-in users are unaffected); config never overwrites it and import never changes the column.

enabled_platform.what: Whether this platform is shown to users (DB is authoritative).
enabled_platform.note: ⚠ When off, users cannot see the platform at all (directory, repo lists, explicit requests answer 403) while internal/script hosting keeps working; config never overwrites it and import never changes the column.

page.channels_hint: Definition fields come from the config file (read-only). This page writes credentials and the enable switch only.
page.platforms_hint: Dialect/endpoints/capabilities come from platform cards and repo-credentials.json (read-only). This page writes the enable switch and bot accounts only.
page.need_one: Fill at least one of client_id / client_secret
page.no_doc: No description yet (add to i18n or config _fields)
page.channels_note: ⚠ Edit configs/oauth-providers.json then restart or re-import.
page.platforms_note: ⚠ Edit config files and re-import; 'enabled' is DB-owned and never overridden by config.
page.bots_note: ⚠ Responses never contain token values; repo-level bindings win over the default account.
page.bots_what: Operating identity and its token (encrypted). At most one is_default per platform.
page.col_drive: Code hosting platforms it can access
page.channels_empty: No OAuth login channel registered yet (they appear after config import)
page.platforms_empty: No repo platform registered yet (they appear after config import)
page.domain_note_channel: Login channel card: OAuth login/binding credentials, decoupled from repo platforms
page.domain_note_platform: Hosting platform card: repo hosting and proxy behavior, decoupled from login channels
page.channels_list_sub: Login channels handle OAuth login and binding. Tap a row for credentials and the code hosting platforms it can access.
page.platforms_list_sub: Code hosting platforms handle repo hosting and proxy behaviour. Tap a row for definition fields, bot accounts and token health.
page.keep_hint: Leave blank to keep the current value
page.self_domain: Same domain: the channel itself is this code hosting platform, so it can access it without any pair.
page.bots_hint: One bot per platform; leave the token blank to keep it. Without a bot, hosting falls back to the user's PAT
page.bots_none_short: no bot (falls back to your PAT)
page.bots_all_inactive: all bots inactive (falls back to your PAT)
page.disable_confirm: Turning off {provider} hides it from users entirely: {repos} repositories, {users} users and {managed} hosted repositories stop being listed (platform credentials of {pats} users are kept). Continue?
